title: Suggestion details drawer: explanations, assumptions, and apply links
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Design and finalize the Suggestions details drawer for the Console beta.

The drawer should help users answer:
1) What is this suggestion and what do we think it saves?
2) Why are we recommending it (what signals are driving it)?
3) What assumptions is the estimate based on, and how fresh/confident is it?
4) How do I apply this safely (deep links + guardrails)?

Scope: Batching + caching suggestions only (beta). Quantization can be referenced as future work but no UI entry/CTA that implies it’s available in this view.

Out of scope: auto-apply flows; contractual savings claims.
content:
## Summary
The Suggestions list gets users to discovery; the details drawer is where trust is won/lost. This design defines the drawer’s structure, key copy patterns, and the deep links/guardrails needed to convert a “looks interesting” click into a safe configuration change.

Beta constraints to keep front-and-center:
- Estimates are directional and based on recent telemetry windows.
- Risk is performance/reliability risk (not security risk).
- No “one click apply” in beta; only navigation to relevant settings + recommended values.

---

## Entry points + layout
**Entry:** Click a row in the Suggestions table (or “View details” in row actions). Drawer opens from the right and preserves the table context.

**Drawer sizing:**
- Default width: 480–560px depending on viewport.
- Scrollable body; header and footer actions remain sticky.

**Sticky header (always visible):**
- Suggestion title: e.g., “Enable continuous batching for /v1/chat (gpt-oss-13b)” or “Increase prefix cache eligibility for /support/tickets”.
- Route + model chips (clickable to open route/model details in new tab).
- Risk badge + tooltip (from DES-640); show as “Low / Medium / High risk”.
- Confidence chip (if available in API): “High / Medium / Low confidence” with tooltip that it reflects data sufficiency + variance.
- “Stale as of” timestamp when `stale_as_of` is present (from compute job); display as “Updated 6h ago” + exact date/time in tooltip.

**Primary metrics band (top of body):**
- Estimated savings: “$X/day (Y%)” + timeframe label (defaults to “based on last 7 days”).
- Estimated latency impact: show p50 and p95 deltas (e.g., “p50 +4ms, p95 +18ms”) and clarify it’s an estimate.
- (Optional if API supplies) Throughput impact: “Max throughput +Z%” or omit entirely in beta to reduce cognitive load.

**Footer actions (sticky):**
- Primary: “Review recommended settings” (jumps to ‘How to apply’ section and highlights values).
- Secondary: “Go to settings” (deep link) with caret menu to choose destination when multiple apply paths exist.
- Tertiary: “Dismiss” with confirmation. Dismiss requires reason picker (optional) + freeform text (optional). Reason list should map to telemetry taxonomy.

---

## Drawer information architecture (sections)
Recommend a single-page scroll with anchors (not tabs) to keep the mental model simple.

### Section 1 — What this changes
A compact “before/after” summary with only the settings relevant to this suggestion.

**Pattern:**
- Setting name
- Current value (from config)
- Recommended value (from suggestion payload)
- Impact note (1 line)

Examples:
- “Max batch tokens: 2048 → 4096”
- “Batching: Off → On (continuous)”
- “Prefix cache eligibility: 0% → 35% of requests (estimated)”

Copy rules:
- Never claim we will set values automatically.
- When current value cannot be fetched (RBAC or config unavailable): show “Current value: unavailable” and keep recommended value visible.

### Section 2 — Why we recommend this
This is the core trust section. It should explain the drivers in human terms and connect to telemetry signals.

**Template:**
- 1–2 sentence “reason” summary
- Bulleted drivers (3–6 max)
- “What could go wrong” callout (ties back to risk label)

**Suggested drivers for batching:**
- “High concurrency during peak (p95 concurrent requests ~N)”
- “Short/medium sequence lengths (median input tokens ~N, output ~N) → batching efficiency”
- “GPU utilization headroom indicates you’re latency-bound by scheduling rather than compute” (only if we have a proxy; otherwise avoid)

**Suggested drivers for caching:**
- “Repeated prefixes detected (top prefix reused across ~N% of requests)”
- “Low current cache hit rate relative to what this traffic pattern supports”
- “Stable prompts (low variation in first N tokens) across calls”

**Risk tie-in (must be explicit):**
- Low risk example: “Your current p95 latency has ample headroom relative to your observed SLO; recommended change is incremental.”
- Medium/high risk examples must name the tradeoff: “This may increase tail latency during spikes if queueing increases.”

### Section 3 — Assumptions & how estimates are computed
Goal: be transparent without overwhelming. Show “show more” disclosure for advanced details.

**Always show (collapsed summary):**
- “Data window: last 7 days (min 48h required)”
- “Traffic sampled: X requests / Y tokens”
- “Pricing inputs: token price from current org plan; excludes discounts/credits” (avoid implying billing parity)
- “Latency model: based on observed queueing + batching overhead; actual results depend on load shape”

**Expandable (advanced):**
- Confidence bands: show as “Expected savings range: $A–$B/day” when available.
- Key parameters used: cache hit uplift assumption, batch efficiency factor.
- Known exclusions: multi-region routing changes, prompt template changes, content-filter overhead, cold-start effects.

**Staleness messaging:**
- If stale > 24h: add a warning inline: “Estimates may be outdated due to telemetry lag. Last updated …” and link to “Telemetry health” page (internal route) if available; otherwise “Learn more” doc link.

### Section 4 — How to apply safely
This section must be explicit: users need to know where to click and what safety rails exist.

**Apply pathways (deep links):**
- “Batching settings” → Console: Project → Optimize/Runtime Settings → Batching
- “Caching settings” → Console: Project → Optimize/Runtime Settings → Caching
- Route-specific overrides → Console: Project → Routes → [route] → Performance
- (If present in their org) Rollouts / policy controls → Console: Project → Rollouts → Policies

**Recommended rollout steps (copy):**
- “Start with a canary (1–5% traffic) for 30–60 minutes.”
- “Watch p95 latency and error rate; revert if regressions exceed your thresholds.”
- “If your route is customer-facing and latency-sensitive, consider Low-risk suggestions first.”

**Guardrails (do/don’t):**
- Do: apply changes during a known traffic window.
- Don’t: combine multiple suggestions at once in beta (keep attribution clear).

**Note on permissions:**
- If user lacks permission to edit settings: show “You have view-only access” + CTA “Copy recommended values” (copies setting/value pairs) and “Request access” (links to internal RBAC flow if in-app; otherwise opens docs).

---

## Dismiss flow
**Purpose:** improve model + reduce noise.

Dismiss confirmation modal fields:
- Reason (required):
  - “Not relevant for this route”
  - “Estimate doesn’t look right”
  - “Too risky right now”
  - “Already implemented another way”
  - “Other”
- Notes (optional)

After dismiss:
- Row disappears from default view.
- Provide filter “Dismissed” to re-open + undo.

---

## Error + empty handling inside drawer
- If suggestion payload loads but deep-linked config page fails: keep drawer content, show “Settings page unavailable” toast.
- If suggestion is no longer valid (backend returns 404 for stable ID): show a state: “This suggestion is no longer available” with CTA to refresh list.
- If key metrics missing: hide that metric card rather than showing zeros; add “Some data unavailable” inline.

---

## Accessibility requirements (for DES-669 follow-up)
- Drawer is a modal dialog with focus trap.
- ESC closes drawer; closing returns focus to the originating row.
- Risk badge tooltip is keyboard accessible and screen-reader labeled.
- All links have descriptive text (avoid “click here”).

---

## Analytics requirements (alignment with ENG-19402)
Events to ensure the drawer is measurable:
- `suggestion_details_opened` with suggestion_id, suggestion_type, route_id, model_id, risk_level, confidence
- `suggestion_details_section_viewed` (optional; only if cheap) for “why”, “assumptions”, “how_to_apply”
- `suggestion_apply_link_clicked` with destination (“batching_settings”, “caching_settings”, “route_override”, “rollouts_policy”)
- `suggestion_dismiss_clicked` + reason

Copy note: keep event naming out of the UI; only for implementation.

---

## Acceptance criteria
- Drawer provides a clear ‘why’ section with 3–6 drivers and a “what could go wrong” tie-in.
- Assumptions section includes data window + pricing/latency caveats with a progressive disclosure.
- Deep links exist for both batching and caching pathways and degrade gracefully if user lacks permissions.
- Drawer includes staleness messaging and does not imply guaranteed savings.
- Copy aligns with risk-level definitions and guidelines (Confluence risk copy doc).

---

## References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimization-suggestions-console-ux-beta-prd.json
- IA/flows: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/suggestions-view-information-architecture-and-user-flows.json
- Risk copy: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/risk-level-definition-and-copy-guidelines.json
- Frontend plan (eng): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/suggestions-view-frontend-implementation-plan.json

---

## Open questions (resolved for beta unless noted)
1) Do we show absolute token counts in the drawer? → Yes, but only in Assumptions (advanced) to reduce intimidation.
2) Do we show confidence as a label? → Yes if API provides; otherwise omit and rely on staleness + assumptions.
3) Should “Go to settings” open in a new tab? → Yes (new tab) to preserve the suggestions context.
4) Should we include rollouts CTA by default? → Only if the org has Rollouts enabled; otherwise provide generic safe-apply steps.
comments: 2026-01-29 — Tessa Morgan: Created ticket to define the drawer IA + copy patterns. Please keep it aligned to beta scope (batching/caching only).
2026-02-01 — Kenji Nakamura: Drafted drawer skeleton (header metrics band + sections). Question: should we use tabs vs scroll sections? Leaning scroll for simplicity.
2026-02-03 — Marissa Cole: Prefer scroll + anchors. Tabs make it harder to notice assumptions; also more implementation complexity for beta.

2026-02-05 — Alicia Perez: Added suggestion to keep metrics band compact; avoid adding throughput unless estimator is robust. Also please ensure staleness is visible if compute lag occurs (we’ve seen telemetry delays).
2026-02-07 — Nora Ahmed: From frontend perspective, sticky header + sticky footer is doable. Need clear guidance on “current vs recommended” layout and empty states for missing current config.
2026-02-09 — Kenji Nakamura: Updated spec with “What this changes” before/after rows and permission-degraded state (copy recommended values).
2026-02-10 — Dr. Maya Srinivasan: Please avoid overstating drivers like GPU utilization unless we have a defensible proxy; focus on observable signals (concurrency, seq length, prefix reuse).
2026-02-11 — Kenji Nakamura: Adjusted ‘Why’ driver list templates to only include signals we can source in v0. Added progressive disclosure for assumptions.

2026-02-12 — George Mbatha: UX research note: testers interpret “risk” as security risk unless we say “performance risk” at least once in the drawer. Recommend adding a one-liner under the badge tooltip or in ‘What could go wrong’.
2026-02-13 — Kenji Nakamura: Incorporated explicit “performance/reliability risk” language in ‘What could go wrong’ callout. Also aligned with risk copy guidelines.
2026-02-14 — Tessa Morgan: Approved direction. Please ensure deep-link destinations match actual Console IA names (Batching/Caching under Runtime Settings).
2026-02-18 — Kenji Nakamura: Final pass after design critique: removed any quantization CTA; kept a single “Future: quantization suggestions” mention in references only.
2026-02-22 — Tessa Morgan: Marking Done. Implementation should follow this spec; any major deviations (tabs, added metrics) should come back through design review.
